title: Almohad Caliphate
capsule: A Berber reform movement turned empire, the Almohads displaced the Almoravids in the 1140s–1170s, ruling from Marrakesh over the Maghreb and al-Andalus. Defeat at Las Navas de Tolosa (1212) broke their Iberian power and opened the great Christian advance.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases (Times Atlas of World History; Kinder & Hilgemann; Shepherd 1926) at ~0.07° resolution. Coastal Maghreb and Andalusi cores are well attested; Saharan limits are conventional lines through thinly governed territory — shown with low confidence. (Almoravid-era shapes share this entry before c. 1150.)
